$schema: Claim/evidence registry for high-stakes research statements. This registry does not replace citations in visible content; it records provenance, evidence class, limitations, and the pages that rely on each claim.

claims.claim: Retrieved consolidated memories can, under some conditions, re-enter a changeable state before being stored again; this is well established in animal research.

sources.citation: Nader K, Schafe GE, LeDoux JE (2000), Nature 406:722-726

claims.limitations: Animal fear-memory research does not by itself establish neural rewriting of emotional beliefs in humans or during psychedelic integration.

claims.claim: Human memory-reconsolidation findings are mixed and the mechanism remains contested.

sources.citation: Chalkia A, Van Oudenhove L, Beckers T (2020), Cortex 129:510-525
Elsey JWB, Van Ast VA, Kindt M (2018), Psychological Bulletin 144(8):797-848

claims.limitations: Evidence does not establish a specific post-psilocybin reconsolidation protocol.

claims.claim: REBUS is an influential theoretical model proposing that psychedelics relax the precision of high-level beliefs.

sources.citation: Carhart-Harris RL, Friston KJ (2019), Pharmacological Reviews 71(3):316-344

claims.limitations: The model is not itself proof that a particular belief changes or that a specific integration practice works.

claims.claim: The published literature does not establish one validated, universally agreed psychedelic-integration protocol or one integration framework proven superior to others.

sources.citation: Bathje GJ, Majeski E, Kudowor M (2022), Frontiers in Psychology 13:824077

claims.limitations: Absence of comparative evidence is not evidence that every integration practice is equally effective or ineffective.

claims.claim: Preclinical work has found structural-plasticity changes after psychedelic exposure in cells and animals.

sources.citation: Ly C et al. (2018), Cell Reports 23(11):3170-3182

claims.limitations: Preclinical plasticity findings do not establish a human therapeutic window or the efficacy of a post-experience practice.
